title: Transfer of a dualizing complex along a finite ring map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] for which $B$ is finitely generated as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Use $D(A)$ and $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on their one-object ringed sites. Let $L\in D(A)$ have finitely generated cohomology in every degree and be isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Assume that the scalar-action map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,L)$ is an isomorphism. Then $\Omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,L)$, regarded as a $B$-complex by the action induced from $(b\varphi)(x)=\varphi(bx)$, has finitely generated $B$-cohomology in every degree, is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $B$-modules, and its scalar-action map $B[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(\Omega_B,\Omega_B)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite; all three conditions expanded using Tag 0A7B, definition-dualizing, and more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: For ordinary modules, restriction $U_0:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ has right adjoint $C_0(I)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I)$ with $(b\varphi)(b')=\varphi(b'b)$. Explicitly the adjunction sends $f:N\to C_0(I)$ to $g:n\mapsto f(n)(1)$, with inverse $g\mapsto(n\mapsto[b\mapsto g(bn)])$. These are linear maps: $f(bn)(1)=(bf(n))(1)=f(n)(b)$, and $g(b'bn)$ verifies $B$-linearity of the inverse; both composites are identities and the formulas commute with pre- and postcomposition. Restriction preserves monomorphisms, since an injective underlying module map remains injective. Thus [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] applied to $U_0\dashv C_0$ proves that each injective $A$-module $I$ gives an injective $B$-module $C_0(I)$.

source.place: Tag 08XR, lemma-hom-injective, used in the first paragraph of Tag 0AX0; ordinary adjunction written out.

proof.text: Choose a bounded complex $I^\bullet$ of injective $A$-modules representing $L$. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Hence [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L)$ by $J^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(B[0],I^\bullet)$. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], this Hom complex with precomposition action represents $C_B(L)\in D(B)$ and has the required underlying $A$-object. Its degree $q$ term is $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I^q)$, injective over $B$ by Step 1, and it vanishes whenever $I^q$ vanishes. Consequently $\Omega_B=C_B(L)$ has a bounded injective $B$-representative $J^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite, first paragraph; Tag 0A70 for the derived coinduction model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-rhom-finite-injective-dimension] with $K=B[0]$ and the given $L$. The Noetherian hypothesis is on $A$, the only nonzero cohomology of $B[0]$ is the finite $A$-module $B$, and $L$ has finite cohomology and a bounded injective representative. Thus every cohomology module of $\Omega_B$ is finite over $A$. Each finite set of $A$-generators also generates as a $B$-module: its $B$-span contains its $A$-span, which is the whole module, by the definition [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. This proves finite $B$-cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, second paragraph (coherence), and Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective.

proof.text: Set $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,L)$ and let $h:A[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be the assumed scalar-action map. For every $n$, the good truncation $\tau_{\le n}B[0]$ is either zero or $B[0]$, so it has bounded-above finite cohomology. It is pseudo-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion]. Apply [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-finite-injective] with $R=A$, $K=B[0]$ and both its targets equal to $L$. Both targets have bounded injective representatives. Moreover $T\cong A[0]$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: the free rank-one complex $A[0]$ itself computes its derived tensor, and $A[0]\otimes_A N[0]=N[0]$. The cited evaluation theorem therefore makes the composite $$B[0]\cong A[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B[0]\xrightarrow{h\otimes1}T\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B[0]\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L),L)$$ an isomorphism. Its transpose is evaluation, by the theorem's stated description: $h(1)=\operatorname{id}_L$, so the subsequent composition into $L$ changes nothing. This composite is precisely the canonical biduality map $\delta_B$.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, canonical biduality proof; more-algebra.tex Tags 066E, 0A67 and 0A69.

proof.text: Write $U:D(B)\to D(A)$ for restriction. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] with its rings $P=A$, $A=B$, its $X=C_B(L)$ and $Y=L$. It identifies $$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B(L),C_B(L))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(U C_B(L),L).$$ By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], the latter is $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L),L)$. Under this identification, the restriction of the scalar-action map sends $b$ to $[\varphi\mapsto(b\varphi)(1)=\varphi(b)]$: indeed the cited internal adjunction sends an endomorphism $f$ to $[\varphi\mapsto f(\varphi)(1)]$. This is the evaluation formula for $\delta_B$ of Step 4 (and $b$ has degree zero, so no sign occurs). Thus the restricted scalar-action map is an isomorphism. Restriction is conservative by [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], so the scalar-action map itself is an isomorphism in $D(B)$. Together with Steps 2 and 3 this proves all three conclusions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q83-119f00ead (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 0AX0 (dualizing.tex:2808) and its proof, and 0A7B/0A5S. The statement is unchanged from live and matches all three dualizing conditions, including the actual scalar-action map. There are no new nodes. Step 1: the U0⊣C0 formulas are correct and restriction preserves monomorphisms, so 015Z (Mathlib leaf) applies. Step 2: the bounded injective I is K-injective, and C_B(L)=Hom^•(B[0],I) is a bounded complex of B-injectives. Step 3: 0G4H with K=B[0] gives finite A-cohomology, so finite B-cohomology. Step 4: the three hypotheses of 0A69 hold (L bounded injective; T≅A[0] has Tor amplitude [0,0]; τ≤n B[0] is 0 or B[0], pseudo-coherent by 066E(2)). The transpose with h(1)=id is b↦(φ↦φ(b)), so δ_B is an isomorphism. Step 5: the general Θ formula f↦(x↦f(x)(1)) sends U(b·id) to δ_B(b); since U is conservative, the scalar-action map is an isomorphism in D(B). Edge cases B=A, B=0, a field extension and DVR→residue field all behave as expected. The grep for 0AX0/0AX1 finds no duplicate, and the cited closures do not contain the item, so there is no cycle. The off-unit tool use of 066E(2) is accepted as a generic black box. Only Stacks is cited, no SGA.
